case_evidence.fact: care sought at a private facility from 11 October (day 4), with Ebola not suspected
laboratory confirmation and isolation on 20 October (T_iso, day 12.5 to 13.5)
alive and described as stable on 20 October

cross_check.note: Shown side by side. The two methods are not averaged, and neither replaces the other. The forecast's value is filled only after this nowcast's precommitment entry.

definitions_differ: The forecast's headline is conditioned on no further case reported by the end of 20 October; this nowcast applies no conditioning, so the forecast's unconditioned value is the closer like-for-like figure.
The forecast counts confirmations dated 21 October to 17 November and reported by 20 November; this nowcast counts reports by the end of 17 November, including any it places on or before 20 October.
This nowcast counts first-generation cases only; the forecast's chain also covers later generations and a small background term for a case from a later importation.

description: Infections the first case in Nigeria has probably already caused, by exposure group, and the confirmed reports they would produce by date. Descriptive; not a calibration row.
disclosures: Rules fixed in a plan before any code or run: sha256 c814e4ddffdc986414d5e3932df38469a940a05b18fba4685e28e651c19c1d6d, registered 2026-10-20T23:21:21Z on the precommitment page reference:bdbv-nigeria-nowcast-precommitment-2026-10-20, with the evidence synthesis sha256 5b3fec30a8da4f05ca456f6d729d3cd400b80f6e95fc1df6dc9e5d716ff9a6b2. No parameter changed after the first full run.

Descriptive context, not a calibration row. It is a second, independent method beside the registered Nigeria case-conditioned forecast and changes nothing in it. The author had not seen any output of that forecast before this nowcast's first run and its precommitment entry; its headline was read afterwards only to fill the N7 cross-check. The two are shown side by side and are not averaged.

Counts are expected numbers under this model: people probably already infected, never people known to be infected. The attack rates are Zaire-species (EBOV) values transferred to Bundibugyo virus, and no Bundibugyo viral-load series exists.

Spec issue S1, resolved before the first run: the daily f(d) table is read with its cumulative column as F at clock time d, so f(0) is a point mass at onset and f(d) is spread over (d-1, d]. This reproduces the evidence synthesis's stated shares for this case (community about 0.24, unsuspected facility about 0.73, after isolation about 0.03 at T_iso 13) and ends the profile at the end of 20 October. The day-of-illness reading, f(d) over [d, d+1), gives about 0.14, 0.79 and 0.07; it is shown as row U1, outside the registered list of 12.
Spec issue S2: isolation-period infections of health workers and caregivers are drawn among those not already infected in the facility window, so no person is counted twice.
Spec issue S3: N4 counts second-generation infections caused before the first case's isolation (T_iso), as the plan's model section defines it, rather than to the end of 20 October.

Spec issue S4: N6 and N7 count confirmed first-generation cases only. The plan gives no timing, listing or detection rules for second-generation infections, so the N4 infections are reported separately and are not in N6, which is low in that respect. A report the model places on or before 20 October is counted from the 21 October row onward; the expected number of such reports is given beside N6. No conditioning on the absence of a further report by 20 October is applied.

Spec issue S5: drawn once per draw are T_iso, w_fatal, v, the precaution scenario and its multiplier (shared by health workers and other patients and visitors), the VHF multiplier (shared by health workers and caregivers), R2, the unlisted share and the detection probability; infection time, incubation, listing, detection and lag are drawn per infected person.
Spec issue S6: no contact was under follow-up before listing began on 20 October, so every first-generation case with onset before T_iso adds second-generation infections under N4.

Spec issue S7: integer ranges are inclusive; the incubation shape (3) is an integer so the Erlang sampler is exact; row S4 is min(2 x U(0.04, 0.20), 0.4); row S10 keeps shape 3 with rate 0.3; N5 tail masses before 8 October and after 17 November are reported separately; 80% bands are the 10th and 90th percentiles of counts across draws; sensitivity rows use the registered seed and 40,000 draws.
Machinery tests were run at small sample sizes before the first full run; they do not produce the registered numbers.

N6 is compared with what Nigeria reports at the registered forecast's coverage review. The comparison is described as a comparison and is never called a hit or a miss; one outcome cannot separate nearby probabilities.

Every exposure count is judgement. The model's mean number of people exposed (about 55 across the groups) is close to the 44 contacts listed on 20 October; the evidence synthesis expects the list to grow, so the exposure counts may be low.
The 80% bands cover parameter uncertainty inside this model only, not model-structure error. Nothing here identifies a person or a facility.

C.note: count 1 to 3 is judgement; attack rate anchored on the published Dean 2016 nursing-care rate

H_direct.note: count 1 to 6 is judgement; attack rate anchored on the published Dean 2016 nursing-care rate 47.9%

H_other.note: count 0 to 10 is judgement; attack rate anchored on the published Dean 2016 no-direct-contact rate 0.8%

O.note: count and attack rate are judgement between Dean 2016's no-direct-contact rate and shared-ward exposure

R2.note: lognormal median 0.8, log-sd 0.6; Faye 2015 published community R 1.4 times a survivor factor

W.note: count 8 to 35 is judgement from Lagos, Dallas and Madrid exposure densities; attack rate anchored on the published Tomori 1999 Kikwit no-barrier rates (nurses 10%, technicians 11%, physicians 31%, others 4%)

clock_and_windows.note: onset, start of facility care and isolation dates from the 20 October statements; T_iso's one-day width is judgement

detection_lags.note: Erlang shape 2; the unlisted mean of 5 days is anchored on the published WHO ERT 2014 onset-to-hospital interval

incubation.note: programme decided prior v0.2.0, gamma(3.0, 0.406), mean 7.39 days, read at run time

infectiousness_profile_f.note: evidence.md A3, constructed on Lanini 2015 peak timing and decay and the WHO ERT 2014 serial interval minus incubation; no Bundibugyo series exists

p_detect.note: 0.85 to 1.0; some cases are mild or never tested

precaution_multipliers.note: programme LEVELS; no published multiplier exists

unlisted_share.note: 0.15 to 0.50, the same range as the registered forecast

v_survivor_viraemia.note: Lanini 2015: survivor peak about 1 log10 lower

w_fatal.note: 0 to 0.3 because the case is alive and stable at day 13

limitations: Second-generation infections after 20 October are not projected; N6 counts first-generation cases only.
The infectiousness profile and every attack rate are EBOV or SUDV values carried across to Bundibugyo virus by assumption.
Exposure counts are judgement; the true facility denominator is unknown.

quantities.N1: expected number and distribution of people infected by the first case, by group: H household and community (days 0 to 4), W health workers at the facility (day 4 to isolation, plus isolation), C the case's own bedside caregivers at the facility, O other patients and visitors
quantities.N2: probability of at least one infection, overall and by group; any_health_worker is group W
quantities.N3: expected number of those infected whose symptoms began by the end of 20 October, before follow-up could detect them
quantities.N4: expected number of second-generation infections caused before the first case's isolation
quantities.N5: expected first-generation onsets by WAT calendar date, 8 October to 17 November
quantities.N6: expected cumulative further confirmed cases reported by the end of each date, 21 October to 17 November, with an 80% band; the checkable quantity
quantities.N7: probability of at least one further confirmed case reported by 17 November under this method, beside the registered forecast's headline

entry_1_first_run.statement: Written before any reviewer had seen the numbers; the run printed only hashes.

sensitivity.label: Health-worker attack rate doubled, capped at 0.4
Survivor viraemia factor v fixed at 1

sensitivity_unregistered.label: Not a registered row; fixed before the first run (spec issue S1). The daily table read as day of illness, f(d) spread over [d, d+1), instead of evidence.md's time-point reading
